long_biography.plain_text:
Political science and business administration prepared Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed Al Nahyan for a career in public service. A son of UAE founder Sheikh Zayed, he moved through foreign affairs and federal government before his appointment as Ruler’s Representative in Al Dhafra. The change turned a national career towards the administration of Abu Dhabi’s western region.

Conservation and humanitarian relief have become durable themes of his public work. As chairman of the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi, he launched a coral-reef rehabilitation programme and has overseen environmental regulation and biodiversity policy. He also chairs Emirates Red Crescent, directing relief and community initiatives including support for orphan care. Together, these roles connect a family legacy of public service with practical work across communities and ecosystems.
